html:
SMTO-POL-0012 — SMTO couldn't save that permission for the waiting action

GUID: f989ac9a-bcfa-474b-b79e-bd4240d1c581
Slug: permission-grant-scope-invalid
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • You chose to allow an action more broadly, but it didn't match the action still waiting for approval, or the conversation no longer exists. No permission was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the conversation. If an Approval needed card is showing, use it; if it's gone, the task has already moved on or stopped. Permission choices apply only to the exact action that is waiting right now.
  2. To allow just this one action, select Approve once. A one-time approval doesn't save a rule, so it can't mismatch the waiting action.
  3. To allow similar actions from now on, use the Allow… menu on the card, or select Open Permissions and edit the rules there. These are the supported ways to save a rule that matches the waiting action.
  4. If the conversation was deleted, start a new conversation and send your request again. A rule for 'This conversation' needs that conversation to still exist.

What success looks like

  • The Approval needed card disappears and the task continues, or the Permissions window shows your new rule.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same choice; it will be refused until it matches the action that is waiting.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A scoped permission grant was rejected: it carried a policy or global scope, its conversation is no longer stored, the run is no longer waiting for that exact approval, or its rule does not match (or is denied for) the pending operation.

What this means

  • A permission amendment must contain one allowable rule or policy and match a retained, unowned pending operation and its conversation scope. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A permission amendment must contain one allowable rule or policy and match a retained, unowned pending operation and its conversation scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare pending-operation identity, retained conversation, grant rule and policy-edit scope; refresh if another owner or decision changed the checkpoint.

How to fix it

  • Reload the run's approval_pending and authority_request, then submit a grant with a single allow rule that matches the pending capability and arguments, scoped to the prompt or an existing conversation (current_run/memory_policy.py amend, permission_scopes.py). Policy-level or global changes go through the Permissions editor, not the approval grant path.
  • Open the owning retained conversation and review its current pending operation. Grant permission only through the supported server-owned editor for that operation and scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The server-owned permission editor accepts a grant matching the exact current operation and intended scope.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
